scope: Theorem 5.11 (A nonzero family with positive coupled index) of the manuscript “Purely cosmetic surgery on knots in the three-sphere” (preprints/Purely-Cosmetic-Surgery-on-Knots-in-the-Three-Sphere-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 306 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 ee916c92b825a868), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 65-66. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix the old caps and their compact probes. Prescribe any lower bounds on the two outside pad lengths, and prescribe any odd evaluations of Λ on their separate extra exceptional classes. There exist arbitrarily large finite stacks with positive bridges at spacing four, satisfying those pad bounds, for which the following hold simultaneously: 65 1. the lifts are those of Lemma 5.2, with a common allowed charge κ and DI = n + z; 2. the actual oriented ordinary family count satisfies Ω ̸= 0; 3. the coupled Dirac index nD = Θ − κ is positive; 4. all auxiliary collars are finite, and the metric and small-data choices can be made to satisfy Theorem 6.1 and Theorem 7.1. The integers specifying the stack and all topological lift data are chosen before the artificial isolation sizes, perturbation bounds, and external Floer gluing lengths.
